questions.q: What is entropy (S) a measure of in a thermodynamic system?
a: The degree of disorder or dispersal of available energy among particles in a system
The total internal heat content of a substance
The speed at which reactant molecules collide
The activation energy barrier of a reaction

questions.q: What condition according to the Third Law of Thermodynamics applies to a perfect crystalline substance at absolute zero (0 Kelvin)?
a: Entropy reaches its maximum possible value

questions.q: How is the standard entropy change of a reaction (Delta S theta) calculated from standard molar entropies (S theta)?
a: Sum of reactant entropies minus sum of product entropies
Product entropies multiplied by reactant entropies
Sum of standard entropies of products minus sum of standard entropies of reactants
Sum of all entropies divided by two

questions.q: Why does the entropy of a substance increase significantly when it melts from a solid to a liquid?
a: Molecules form a rigid crystal lattice
Particles gain freedom of movement, leading to greater disorder and more ways of distributing energy

questions.q: What is the sign of Delta S for the reaction: N<sub>2</sub> (g) + 3H<sub>2</sub> (g) <-> 2NH<sub>3</sub> (g)?
a: Negative (decrease in entropy because 4 moles of gas form 2 moles of gas)

questions.q: What does Gibbs free energy change (Delta G) determine regarding a chemical reaction?
a: The rate at which products are formed
Whether a chemical reaction is thermodynamically spontaneous or feasible
The exact activation energy of the process

questions.q: What is the mathematical equation relating Gibbs free energy change (Delta G), enthalpy change (Delta H), and entropy change (Delta S) at constant temperature (T)?
a: Delta G equals Delta H plus T Delta S
Delta G equals Delta H multiplied by T Delta S
Delta G equals Delta H minus T Delta S
Delta G equals T Delta H minus Delta S

questions.q: What condition must be met for a chemical reaction or process to be thermodynamically feasible (spontaneous)?
a: Delta S of surroundings must be negative
Delta G must be zero or negative (Delta G <= 0)

questions.q: Why might an endothermic reaction (Delta H > 0) still be spontaneous at high temperatures?
a: If Delta S is positive and large enough such that the T Delta S term exceeds Delta H, making Delta G negative
Because endothermic reactions always release energy at high pressure
Because entropy decreases at high temperatures

questions.q: What is the unit of standard molar entropy (S theta) as reported in thermodynamic tables?
What happens to the entropy of the surroundings when an exothermic reaction occurs in a system?
a: Surroundings entropy increases because thermal energy released increases the thermal disorder of the surroundings

questions.q: What temperature (T) threshold determines when a reaction with both positive Delta H and positive Delta S becomes spontaneous?
a: Above a certain temperature where T Delta S exceeds Delta H, making Delta G negative

questions.q: What is the sign of Delta S for the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate: CaCO<sub>3</sub> (s) -> CaO (s) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g)?
a: Positive (because a gas is produced from a solid, increasing disorder)

questions.q: What does a negative value of Gibbs free energy change (Delta G) signify?
a: The reaction is thermodynamically feasible / spontaneous under the specified conditions

questions.q: How is the entropy change of the surroundings (Delta S_surrounding) calculated from the enthalpy change of the reaction (Delta H) and temperature (T)?
a: Delta S_surrounding equals Delta H multiplied by T
Delta S_surrounding equals T divided by Delta H
Delta S_surrounding equals negative Delta H divided by T (-Delta H / T)
Delta S_surrounding equals Delta H plus T

questions.q: Why does water freezing into ice at -10 degrees Celsius occur spontaneously even though it involves a decrease in system entropy?
a: Ice has higher energy than water

The entropy of the system decreases, but the exothermic heat released to the surroundings increases the entropy of the surroundings by a greater amount, resulting in a net increase in total entropy (Delta G < 0)

questions.q: What is the physical state change that typically results in the largest increase in entropy for a given substance?
At what condition of Delta G is a chemical system considered to be at dynamic equilibrium?
a: Delta G is a large positive number
Delta G is exactly equal to zero

questions.q: How does an increase in the number of moles of gas from reactants to products affect the entropy change of the system (Delta S)?
a: Has no effect on Delta S
Increases Delta S because gases have significantly higher molar entropies than liquids or solids

questions.q: What is the primary factor that prevents a reaction with negative Delta H and negative Delta S from being spontaneous at extremely high temperatures?
a: The -T Delta S term becomes large and positive, overcoming the negative Delta H and making Delta G positive

questions.q: Which of the following substances would you expect to have the highest standard molar entropy (S theta) at 298 Kelvin?
What equation links the standard Gibbs free energy change of a reaction (Delta G theta) to its equilibrium constant (Kc or Kp)?
a: Delta G theta equals RT multiplied by Kc
Delta G theta equals negative RT ln(K) (-RT ln K)
Delta G theta equals K divided by RT
Delta G theta equals exp(-RT / K)

questions.q: What is total entropy change (Delta S_total) equal to according to the Second Law of Thermodynamics for a spontaneous process?
a: Delta S_total equals system entropy minus surroundings entropy
Delta S_total equals Delta S_system plus Delta S_surroundings, and must be positive for a spontaneous process
Delta S_total equals enthalpy change divided by temperature

questions.q: Why are some reactions that are thermodynamically feasible (Delta G < 0) practically very slow or imperceptible at room temperature?
a: Because Gibbs free energy is positive
Because thermodynamics only indicates feasibility, not kinetics or activation energy barriers

questions.q: What is the sign of Delta S for the dissolution of solid ammonium nitrate in water?
a: Positive because solid crystal lattice breaks apart into freely moving aqueous ions, increasing disorder
Negative because water orders around ions

questions.q: How does temperature affect the value of the T Delta S term in the Gibbs free energy equation?
a: It increases the magnitude of the term proportionally
It makes the term negative at all temperatures

questions.q: What does a reaction with a positive Delta H and a positive Delta S require to become spontaneous?
a: Temperatures high enough so that T Delta S is greater than Delta H
A catalyst to alter Delta H
